key_insight: Halide substitution in Ca$_3$PX$_3$ perovskites strongly tunes stability, bandgap, and photovoltaic performance, with Ca$_3$PI$_3$ emerging as the best solar-cell candidate.
engineering_relevance: These results identify a compositional route to optimize lead-free perovskite absorbers for higher-efficiency solar cell and optoelectronic device design.
method: First-principles calculations of structural and electronic properties
Band-structure and optical analysis across X = F, Cl, Br, I
SLME-based photovoltaic screening to compare solar-cell potential
evidence_signal: The abstract reports direct bandgaps spanning 2.0–3.788 eV and SLME values ranging from 0.6% for Ca$_3$PF$_3$ to 29.6% for Ca$_3$PI$_3$.
watch_item: High predicted efficiency alone does not guarantee device viability; experimental synthesis, stability, and charge-transport performance still need validation.
paper_title: Halide substitution effects on the photovoltaic properties of Ca$_3$PX$_3$ (X = F, Cl, Br, I) perovskites: advancing solar cell efficiency
